findings.title: Provider-home ancestor ownership rejects every normal first Settings operation for operator UID different from 65532
findings.concrete_input_and_timing: Fresh p4a-settings-offline installation via normal installer, mapped operator UID=1000, first explicit Settings save/read after OPEN. Installer supplies no RUNTIME_UID/RUNTIME_GID build args. Image defaults are 65532 and Dockerfile recursively chowns /state to 65532. Overlay runs as UID/GID of operator and binds only /runtime and /state/provider, leaving /state owned by 65532.
findings.mechanism: The provider bind is correctly current-UID/mode0700, but RuntimeHost._settings_native calls private_paths.directory(root) before spawning management. Ancestor /state has UID65532, outside {0,current UID}; guard raises ValueError("Replaceable ancestor"). _settings_run catches it and latches management_failed=True with INDETERMINATE. Native config is never reached; subsequent operations in that boot are blocked. This is introduced by composing the new normal installed profile with the unchanged image/validator, not a reopening of earlier management-config findings.

observed.boundary: SOURCE image-filesystem metadata double; no OCI, native import or boot

findings.positive_control: Same provider UID/mode, but /state UID0 or current UID: real directory guard ACCEPTED. Shipped UID65532: Replaceable ancestor. Actual unmodified Settings coroutine under this stat seam: INDETERMINATE/management_failed=true/native_spawns=0.
findings.minimal_fix: Keep immutable /state root-owned and traversable in the native image while preserving the mapped operator-owned private provider bind; adjust only required distribution ownership after existing chown and reseal Dockerfile/bundle/image. Do not weaken ancestor guard, run as root, adopt personal auth or add another launcher. Preserve inert child-directory requirements.
findings.required_regression: Exercise image ancestor ownership with mapped UID through the existing Settings consumer. After focused review, real normal install/start/save/readback/Stop/freshStart/read proves persistence; a temporary same-owner home alone is insufficient.
